title: state the fixed first-right-then-down split rule in the herding docs
verify: .bee/bin/bee dev regen && .bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --check && rg -n 'wider than tall' skills docs | wc -l
action: The pane-split geometry rule changes from an aspect-ratio choice to a FIXED strategy, because sub-dividing width made three worker panes unreadable. New rule: the FIRST split of a tab goes `--direction right` (one worker gets the full-height column); EVERY later split goes `--direction down`, so extra workers stack as full-width horizontal bands and width halves at most once. Ratio stays 0.5. Parent pane choice stays the roomiest pane (largest rect.width * rect.height). Edit skills/bee-herding/references/role-dispatch.md section 8 step 2 (around lines 324-335): replace the 'take the pane with the largest rect.width * rect.height, and pass --direction right if it is wider than tall, else --direction down' sentence with the fixed rule — still read `herdr pane layout --pane <any runtime pane_id>`, still split the largest-area pane, but choose the direction from how many panes that layout lists: exactly one pane (the untouched runtime root) -> `--direction right`, two or more -> `--direction down`. Say in one line WHY: a down split leaves width unchanged, so worker panes stay wide enough to read and wide enough for herdr to accept a submitted prompt (a right split halves width every time, which is what made the third pane unusable). Update the summary table row near line 472 to match. In skills/bee-herding/references/wave-runs.md (around line 28) the example hardcodes `--direction right`; keep the example but add that the direction follows role-dispatch.md section 8's fixed rule (right only for a tab's first split, down after that). In docs/knowledge/areas/bee-herding/agent-resolution-and-spawn-commands.md, sync whatever it says about the split direction to the same rule; if it says nothing about direction, add one short line stating it. Do NOT edit skills/bee-herding/references/spawn-proof.md — it is a recorded live observation, not a rule, and its own split was a first split, so it stays true. Run `.bee/bin/bee dev regen` after the edits so the generated registry payload carries the new skill text.
